recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Do not duplicate the rule on the HTTP page or in search.html#all unless the work group requests a navigation-only editorial change, because the current Search Inputs section already conveys the requested behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-20392 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It requested explicit FHIR-core search/http language stating that a search such as GET [base]/[type] with no filters returns all resources of that type, and that servers unable or unwilling to run such a search should return an error instead of silently applying a default filter.
initial_application: The behavior was introduced into source/search.html before this tracker was named in git history by 142ad7624c, then explicitly reconciled for FHIR-20392 by 6600a9d173 on 2022-08-08. The FHIR-20392 commit expanded the examples to system/type GET and POST searches, added the search-context scope qualifier, and added overly-broad error guidance.
additional_context: The linked 2019 Zulip discussion confirms that searches without filters are allowed, that authorization can constrain visible records, and that a server can reject an overly broad search. Later source edits a3766ac36c6 and 887bc2383fb only changed conformance markup and punctuation around the paragraph. Confluence searches found no conflicting minutes.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/search.html lines 232-235 already say that searches without filters, including GET [base], GET [base]/Patient, and POST _search forms with no body, SHOULD return all records in scope of the search context and MAY be rejected as overly broad with an appropriate error.
